notes:
Shorthand notes from calls. Customer: high-perf RTB stack; main ask = shave ~30% per-request cost while keeping p95 < 70ms. Currently using in-house PyTorch endpoints on GPUs (mixed V100 + A10); want ability to route to cheaper quantized variants under load. Interested in: smart batching without increasing tail latency, automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated user contexts, and quantization tradeoffs (int8 vs 4-bit) for model family they plan to use (open LLaMA-derivative). Quote: 'We can't accept a 200ms tail — advertisers lose auctions.'

POC acceptance criteria (as discussed):
  - Reranking endpoint must hit p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 70ms at steady-state 200 req/s.
  - Burst handling to 1k qps for 30s without error spike >0.5%.
  - Token-level cost reduction >=25% vs current baseline using batching + quantized runtime.
  - Demo of KV cache improving average tokens-per-request by >=15% for repeated prefixes.

They asked for a perf spreadsheet and guidance on kernel/sequence-length choices — sending Redwood perf plan and benchmark template. SE note: consider testing both continuous batching and small fixed-window batching; instrument with latency budgets per shard.
